title: The Impact of Education on Chronic Disease Risk

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
We will use an Instrumental Variable (IV) approach for this analysis. The level of education (x) could potentially be endogenous due to omitted variable bias or reverse causality. To identify the causal effect of education on chronic disease incidence (y), we utilize the quarter-of-birth (z) as an instrumental variable. 

The key assumptions here are:
- Relevance: The quarter-of-birth (z) is correlated with years of education (x).
- Exogeneity: The quarter-of-birth (z) affects the likelihood of developing chronic disease (y) only through its effect on education (x), not directly or through omitted variables that also affect y.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(AER) # for IV regression
library(lmtest) # for heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors
library(sandwich) # for robust covariance matrix

# Load the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s72_data.csv", header = TRUE)

# First stage regression: check relevance of the instrument
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = data)
summary(first_stage)

# Perform the IV regression
iv_model <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data)

# Display the main results
summary(iv_model, vcov = sandwich) # robust standard errors

# Robustness checks
# 1. Test for weak instrument
first_stage_fstat <- summary(first_stage)$fstatistic[1]
cat("First-stage F-statistic:", first_stage_fstat, "\n")

# 2. Overidentification test
# This analysis is limited to just one instrument and one endogenous regressor so this does not apply directly.

# Print the coefficient of interest
cat("IV estimate of education on chronic disease:", coef(summary(iv_model, vcov = sandwich))["x", "Estimate"], "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
The expected sign of the education coefficient is negative, suggesting that higher levels of education reduce the likelihood of developing chronic diseases. The magnitude will depend on the strength of the effect and the data's specific circumstances, but we anticipate that it will be economically and statistically significant based on literature linking educational attainment to better health outcomes. Given the instrumental variable approach, we need to check for the strength of the instrument to ensure valid inference. If valid, the findings should reflect the causal impact of education corrected for endogeneity.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Quarter-of-birth serves as an instrument for education.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Higher educational attainment significantly reduces the risk of chronic diseases.
